item.text:
**Bottom line:** Mixed, leaning positive on monetary credibility and near-term market stability, but negative on fiscal prudence and long-term investment conditions. AMLO’s team kept technocratic macro management largely intact, yet 2024 also saw procyclical fiscal pressure, heavy Pemex support, and investor चिंता around weakening checks and courts.

- [Mexican finance minister seeks to soothe investors, reduce public debt](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/mexican-finance-minister-seeks-to-soothe-investors-reduce-public-debt-3470241) | Reuters | 2024-06-04 | Rogelio Ramírez de la O stayed on, promised debt reduction and fiscal discipline, pledged to refresh communication with investors and rating agencies, and explicitly backed central bank autonomy, rule of law, and private investment. IDs: `5B.3`, `5B.2`, `5B.1`

- [Mexico: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2024 Article IV Mission](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/10/15/mcs-mexico-staff-concluding-statement-of-the-2024-aiv-mission) | IMF | 2024-10-15 | Positive and negative in one source: the IMF said inflation pressures were receding, monetary policy remained well calibrated, and Mexico’s frameworks were very strong, but it also said 2024 fiscal policy was procyclical, the deficit was likely to widen sharply, Pemex support was costly, and credible medium-term consolidation was needed. IDs: `5B.3`, `5B.1`

- [Informe trimestral abr-jun 2024, resumen visual](https://www.banxico.org.mx/publicaciones-y-prensa/resumenes-visuales/informe-trimestral-html/informe-trimestral-abr-jun-00003.html) | Banco de México | 2024-08-28 | Banxico kept policy tight through mid-2024, then lowered rates only as inflation continued easing, while reaffirming that policy remained oriented to the 3 percent inflation target and a low-stable-inflation environment. This supports monetary credibility. IDs: `5B.3`

- [200 puntos del sexto informe de gobierno](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/200-puntos-del-sexto-informe-de-gobierno/) | Presidencia de México | 2024-09-01 | AMLO’s own end-of-term report claimed gains in inflation, debt, investment, poverty reduction, and public programs. This is positive evidence for his intended macroeconomic narrative, but it is self-reporting rather than independent validation. IDs: `5B.3`, `5B.1`

- [Analysis-Mexico investors worry lopsided vote could threaten rule of law](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/analysismexico-investors-worry-lopsided-vote-could-threaten-rule-of-law-3475796) | Reuters | 2024-06-07 | Investors feared AMLO might use his post-election mandate to sweep aside checks on presidential power in his final month, which would raise long-term policy and investment risk even if macro indicators were still functioning. IDs: `5B.3`, `4B.10`

- [Moody's cuts indebted oil firm Pemex's rating by two notches to B3](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/moodys-cuts-indebted-oil-firm-033156859.html) | Reuters | 2024-02-09 | Moody’s said Pemex faced poorer credit quality and that expected government support could be strained by 2024 fiscal deterioration, higher borrowing costs, social spending, and flagship projects. That is strong negative evidence on fiscal responsibility. IDs: `5B.3`, `5B.1`

- [Mexicos sweeping judicial overhaul formally takes effect](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-sweeping-judicial-overhaul-formally-takes-effect-3616588) | Reuters | 2024-09-15 | Reuters reported the constitutional overhaul was enacted amid criticism that it weakened judicial independence and investor confidence. That is negative evidence for long-term investment conditions, even if it is not a pure macro indicator. IDs: `5B.3`, `4B.10`

**Search gap:** I did not find direct 2024 evidence that AMLO himself overruled Banxico, imposed capital controls, or triggered a hard macro crisis. The strongest negatives are instead fiscal slippage, Pemex support, and investor concern about rule-of-law erosion.
